subject: English L1
title: Unit 4: Past Simple and Time Clauses

A.q: When I _____ ten years old, I _____ tennis.
A.explain: Was / played is correct: I takes was, and played is the simple past. Were is plural, and play is present.

A.q: My grandparents always _____ fresh bread at home when I was little.
A.explain: Had is the simple past, and when I was little marks the past. Have is present plural, has is present singular, and having is a participle.

A.q: My parents and I _____ at the airport very early yesterday morning.
A.explain: Plural subject needs were, and yesterday morning marks the past. Was is singular, are is present, and been needs a helping verb.

A.q: The glass _____ when it hit the floor.
A.explain: Broke is simple past. Break is present, broken is a participle, and breaking is continuous.

A.q: During the last mission, the astronauts _____ their pens float in microgravity.
A.explain: Watched is simple past, and during the last mission marks the past. Watch is present, watching is continuous, and watches is third-person present.

A.q: When the principal _____ to the hall, the students stopped talking.
A.explain: Came is simple past in the time clause. Come is present, comes is third-person present, and coming is continuous.

A.q: The audience _____ upset when the singer canceled the show.
A.explain: Got is simple past. Get is present, gets is third-person present, and getting is continuous.

A.q: We _____ when a cat suddenly ran across the road.
A.explain: Screamed is simple past. Scream is present, screaming is continuous, and screams is third-person present.

A.q: I _____ on the report all morning before my manager called.
A.explain: Worked is simple past. Work is present, working is continuous, and works is third-person present.

A.q: The chef _____ the soup before the restaurant opened.
A.explain: Cooked is simple past. Cook is present, cooking is continuous, and cooks is third-person present.

A.q: When the crew _____ a leak in the oxygen tank, they began repairs.
A.explain: Detected is simple past. Detect is present, detecting is continuous, and detects is third-person present.

A.q: Correct: When you start working at the clinic?
options: When did you start working at the clinic?
When you started working at the clinic?
When did you started working at the clinic?
When you start working at the clinic?
A.explain: Questions need did + base verb. Missing did, did + started, and the bare question form are wrong.

A.q: Correct: Did you finished your homework last night?
options: Did you finish your homework last night?
Did you finished your homework last night?
Did you finishes your homework last night?
You finished your homework last night?
A.explain: Did + base verb is correct. Did + finished is double past.

A.q: Correct: The nurse check my temperature yesterday.
options: The nurse checked my temperature yesterday
The nurse check my temperature yesterday
The nurse checks my temperature yesterday
The nurse checking my temperature yesterday
A.explain: Checked is simple past. Check is present, checks is third-person present, and checking is continuous.

A.q: Correct: Last year our class take a trip to the museum.
options: Last year our class took a trip to the museum
Last year our class take a trip to the museum
Last year our class takes a trip to the museum
Last year our class taking a trip to the museum
A.explain: Took is simple past. Take is present, takes is third person, and taking is continuous.

A.q: Correct: The clinic open a new waiting room last month.
options: The clinic opened a new waiting room last month
The clinic open a new waiting room last month
The clinic opens a new waiting room last month
The clinic opening a new waiting room last month
A.explain: Opened is simple past. Open is present, opens is third-person present, and opening is continuous.

A.q: Correct: We don't needed a referral for the blood test last month.
options: We didn't need a referral for the blood test last month
We don't needed a referral for the blood test last month
We didn't needed a referral for the blood test last month
We don't need a referral for the blood test last month
A.explain: Didn't + base verb need is correct past negative. Don't needed mixes present and past, didn't needed is double past, and don't need is present.

A.q: Correct: The patient didn't went to the clinic after the checkup.
options: The patient didn't go to the clinic after the checkup
The patient didn't went to the clinic after the checkup
The patient don't go to the clinic after the checkup
The patient wasn't go to the clinic after the checkup
A.explain: Didn't + base verb go is correct. Didn't went is double past, don't go is present, and wasn't go is not a past negative form.

A.q: Correct: We wasn't surprised when the results came out.
options: We weren't surprised when the results came out
We wasn't surprised when the results came out
We aren't surprised when the results came out
We didn't surprised when the results came out
A.explain: Plural needs weren't. Wasn't is singular, aren't is present, and didn't surprised is incorrect.

A.q: Which time-clause pair is both in simple past?
options: They left the house when the rain stopped
They leave the house when the rain stopped
They left the house when the rain stop
They leaving the house when the rain stopped
A.explain: Both verbs need simple past: left and stopped. Leave and stop are present, and leaving is continuous.

A.q: Which sentence uses the correct plural past form?
options: The astronauts were in microgravity for six months
The astronauts was in microgravity for six months
The astronauts are in microgravity for six months
The astronauts been in microgravity for six months
A.explain: Were is correct for the plural subject the astronauts. Was is singular, are is present, and been needs a helping verb.

A.q: Which time-clause sentence uses simple past after before?
options: She locked the door before she left the office
She lock the door before she left the office
She locked the door before she leave the office
She locking the door before she left the office
A.explain: Both verbs need simple past: locked and left. Lock and leave are present, and locking is continuous.

A.q: Which question avoids double past?
options: Did you enjoy the film last night?
Did you enjoyed the film last night?
Do you enjoy the film last night?
You enjoyed the film last night?
A.explain: Did + base verb enjoy is correct. Did + enjoyed is double past, do is present, and the last option lacks the auxiliary.

A.q: Which negative past avoids double marking?
A.explain: Didn't + base verb is correct. Didn't ate is double past. Don't eat is present. Wasn't eat is incorrect.

A.q: Which plural form is correct with past be?
options: The ships weren't ready when the storm arrived
The ships wasn't ready when the storm arrived
The ships aren't ready when the storm arrived
The ships didn't ready when the storm arrived
A.explain: Weren't is correct for plural ships. Wasn't is singular, aren't is present, and didn't ready is missing a main verb.

A.q: Which simple-past form fits the time clause when?
options: We shouted when a cat suddenly ran across the road
We shout when a cat suddenly ran across the road
We shouting when a cat suddenly ran across the road
We shouts when a cat suddenly ran across the road
A.explain: Shouted is simple past. Shout is present, shouting is continuous, and shouts is third-person present.

A.q: Which sentence describes a completed past action?
options: The shop opened a new section last month
The shop open a new section last month
The shop opens a new section last month
The shop opening a new section last month
A.explain: Opened is simple past. Open is present, opens is third-person present, and opening is continuous.

A.q: Which time-clause verb after after is simple past?
options: I called my brother after I finished my homework
I call my brother after I finished my homework
I calling my brother after I finished my homework
I calls my brother after I finished my homework
A.explain: Called is simple past. Call is present, calling is continuous, and calls is third-person present.

A.q: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Yesterday the receptionist answered forty phone calls
Yesterday the receptionist answer forty phone calls
Yesterday the receptionist answers forty phone calls
Yesterday the receptionist answering forty phone calls
A.explain: Answered is simple past. Answer is present, answers is third-person present, and answering is continuous.

A.q: Last night, ___ a serious fire in the old market.
A.explain: There was is correct because a serious fire is singular. There were is plural, was there is question order, and were there is plural question order.

A.q: ___ many visitors at the museum?
A.explain: Were there is correct for a plural question about visitors. There were is statement order, was there is singular, and there was is singular statement order.

A.q: Were there many visitors at the museum? Yes, ___.
A.explain: There were repeats the plural there construction. There was is singular, they were changes the subject, and they was is wrong for plural.

A.q: My cousins ___ at my flat last weekend.
A.explain: Cousins is plural and the time is last weekend, so were all is correct. Was all is singular, are all is present, and been all needs a helping verb.

A.q: I ___ time to call you yesterday.
A.explain: Didn't have is correct past negative. Don't have is present, haven't had is present perfect, and didn't had is double past.

A.q: What ___ he ___ at the meeting yesterday?
A.explain: Did / say is correct: did + subject + base verb. Do / say is present, did / said is double past, and are / saying is present continuous.

A.q: Which question matches: My cousins were at the wedding yesterday.
A.explain: Cousins is plural, so the past be verb is were. Where was is singular, where are is present, and where did needs a main verb.

A.q: The campfire burned ___ sunrise.
A.explain: Until marks the endpoint of the continued burning. While needs a clause with another ongoing action, as soon as marks an immediate point, and since marks a start.

A.q: When I ___ a poor mark on the test, I decided to study harder.
A.explain: Got is simple past. Get is present, getting is continuous, and was get is not a valid past form.

A.q: Alexander Fleming ___ penicillin in 1928.
A.explain: Discovered is simple past for a single event. Uses to is present, discovering is a participle, and used to marks repeated past habits.

A.q: The reaction _____ when the two chemicals were mixed.
A.explain: Began is simple past. Begin is present, begun is a participle, and beginning is continuous.
